skill.name: supabase-automation
skill.description: Automate Supabase queries, schema inspection, project administration, storage, edge functions, service checks, and SQL execution through Rube MCP.
skill.summary: Operate Supabase databases, projects, storage, functions, and configurations through the Rube MCP integration.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All 112 external-command detections are false positives caused by Markdown inline-code formatting; the file contains no executable shell or Ruby code. The skill directs clients to a third-party MCP endpoint and can retrieve live Supabase keys. It also permits arbitrary SQL writes without mandatory confirmation, requiring strong approval and secret-handling controls.

remediation.issue: Database mutations can run without a mandatory approval gate.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before non-read-only SQL, and show the target project, expected impact, and rollback plan.

remediation.issue: The API-key tool can return live service-role credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Require a stated need before key retrieval, never return full values, and recommend scoped or rotated credentials.

remediation.issue: Supabase operations pass through an external MCP service.
remediation.suggestion: Document Rube and Composio as external processors, require endpoint verification, and explain what Supabase data may transit them.

content.user_title: Automate Supabase Operations with Rube MCP
content.value_statement: Supabase administration often requires several tools and careful sequencing. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rube MCP workflows for data, projects, storage, and health checks.
actual_capabilities: Connects a Supabase account through Rube MCP and checks connection status.
Lists projects, organizations, members, tables, views, storage buckets, database branches, and edge functions.
Inspects table schemas, relationships, indexes, database configuration, authentication settings, and service health.
Queries table data with filters, sorting, selected columns, offsets, and limits.
Runs PostgreSQL statements for complex reads and authorized data changes.
Generates TypeScript types for selected database schemas.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP, a connected Supabase account, and sufficient project permissions.
Can retrieve sensitive project keys and can execute destructive SQL.
Edge function tools inspect metadata but cannot create or deploy functions.
Storage tools primarily list buckets; direct file operations may require a separate proxy call.

use_cases.title: Inspect Application Data
use_cases.description: Explore tables, inspect schemas, and run filtered read-only queries before implementing application changes.

use_cases.title: Plan Database Changes
use_cases.description: Review relationships and indexes, prepare controlled SQL changes, and verify results after approval.

use_cases.title: Monitor Supabase Projects
use_cases.description: Inventory projects, review configurations, inspect organization access, and check service health across an account.

prompt_templates.title: List My Projects
prompt_templates.prompt: Connect to my Supabase account through Rube MCP. List available projects and summarize each project without changing anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a read-only account inventory.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect and Query a Table
prompt_templates.prompt: Find project [project name]. Inspect [schema.table], then return [columns] where [condition]. Use read-only mode and limit results to [number].
prompt_templates.scenario: Inspect a schema before running a filtered query.

prompt_templates.title: Check Project Services
prompt_templates.prompt: Check [project name] service health for auth, database, REST, realtime, and storage. Summarize failures and permission errors without retrieving API keys.
prompt_templates.scenario: Investigate service availability without exposing credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare and Apply a Database Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [schema.table], then prepare SQL for [change]. Explain impact and rollback steps. Wait for approval before execution, then verify the result.
prompt_templates.scenario: Apply an advanced mutation with explicit review and verification.

output_examples.input: List my Supabase projects and identify the project named Billing.
output: No project settings or data were changed.

output_examples.input: Inspect the public invoices table and summarize its structure.
output: The table contains invoice identifiers, customer references, amounts, statuses, and timestamps.
Customer references use a foreign key.
Two indexes support customer and status lookups.

output_examples.input: Check health for the authentication, database, and storage services.
output_examples.output: Authentication and database services are healthy. Storage reports degraded status and should be reviewed before file operations.

best_practices: Use current tool schemas from RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS before every workflow.
Inspect table schemas before writes and use read-only mode for every SELECT query.
Require explicit approval for mutations and mask every returned secret.
anti_patterns: Do not retrieve API keys unless the task specifically requires them.
Do not run generated SQL before reviewing the target project, impact, and rollback plan.
Do not assume the public schema, table names, permissions, or service availability.

faq.question: What do I need before using this skill?
faq.answer: Configure the Rube MCP endpoint, connect Supabase, and grant only the permissions required for the task.

faq.question: Can this skill change database data?
faq.answer: Yes. It can run SQL for inserts, updates, deletes, and schema changes when the connected account permits them.

faq.question: Can it work in read-only mode?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the table selection tool or enable read-only mode for SQL queries.

faq.question: Does it expose Supabase API keys?
faq.answer: It can retrieve live keys. Request them only when necessary, and always mask full values in outputs.

faq.question: Can it deploy edge functions?
faq.answer: No. The documented edge function tools list functions and retrieve metadata, but they do not create or deploy functions.

faq.question: Why must tool schemas be searched first?
faq.answer: Rube tool names and parameters can change. Searching first provides the current schema and reduces invalid calls.
